title: AI Doc Review — Physician in the Middle
rulesTable: HARD TRIGGERS (bypass reliability): STEMI, stroke, unstable vitals (SBP<90/HR>130/SpO2<90), new AMS → escalate immediately; physician acknowledges
Reliability states per field: Reliable / Not said / Said wrong / Said differently on purpose
Score is context-dependent: sensitive topic, companion present, interpreter, adolescent, age≥75 without companion, low literacy, inconsistency with records/transcript
If-wrong: dangerous alternative → risk range = P(alt)×severity; ddx widens; plan changes
Ground truth: true ESI/plan from hidden truth (e.g. pregnant+abd pain → ESI 2 + escalate; methadone + azithro/FQ → modify plan)
VOI = P(field wrong) × plan change × miss severity; top 3 'ask next'

glossary.Reliable: The reported value is consistent with context and records; likely true.
glossary.Not said: Omission — including never asked. See 'expected questions not asked' for this complaint.
glossary.Said wrong: Unintentional error: recall error, misunderstanding, or answered a different question (e.g. via interpreter).
glossary.Said differently on purpose: Deliberate reframing due to stigma, fear, culture, language or health literacy — substance use, safety at home, adherence, minimized symptoms, pregnancy, sexual history.
glossary.reliability score: 0–100% confidence the stated value is true, from context (age, companion, interpreter, setting, topic sensitivity) and consistency with other fields/records.
glossary.if wrong: If this field is wrong: the dangerous alternative, the serious-miss risk range (P(alt) × severity), the worst-case miss and how the plan changes.
glossary.VOI: Value of information = P(field wrong) × expected plan change × miss severity. Higher = ask first.
glossary.ask next: Send one question to the patient; the answer updates the encounter and re-scores reliability, risk and VOI.
glossary.re-rate: Physician overrides the field's reliability state (R/N/W/D). Logged as a training label.
glossary.hard trigger: MI/STEMI, stroke, unstable vitals, AMS: escalation fires immediately and the reliability analysis is bypassed. The physician acknowledges.
glossary.recommend escalation: A severe miss can't be excluded and the information is unreliable: escalate rather than sign off.
glossary.confidence: The AI's self-reported confidence in its proposal.
glossary.priority: Queue order: uncertainty × error cost + wait + if-wrong risk + hard triggers (top).
glossary.census: ED rooms occupied/total per area; context for escalation.
glossary.boarding: Admitted patients still occupying ED rooms.
glossary.high error cost: A wrong answer on this link is costly.
glossary.auto-pass: Confident, low-cost items with no high-severity reason are passed automatically; a sample goes to spot-check.
glossary.spot-check: A random sample of auto-passed items for physician review.
glossary.what happens next: Downstream effect if you pass or change this proposal.
glossary.AI differential (with uncertainty): Ranges widen where a low-reliability field could change the diagnosis.
glossary.Expected questions not asked: Complaint-specific checklist of questions the AI never asked.
glossary.trial category: A reviewer-added category; logged but never changes routing until promoted.
glossary.BN: Analysis from the local Bayesian-network sidecar (risk_engine, exact inference). Parameters are PLACEHOLDER values pending expert review; labels (very unlikely/unlikely/possible/likely) matter more than the digits.
glossary.fallback: Sidecar unreachable or complaint not modelled: Swift heuristic reliability/risk (not a probabilistic model).
